item.title: China's top diplomat calls for new "golden decade" of Lancang-Mekong cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
China's top diplomat calls for new "golden decade" of Lancang-Mekong cooperation Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, co-chairs the 11th Lancang-Mekong Cooperation (LMC) Foreign Ministers' Meeting with Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 4, 2026. Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn, Lao Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Thongsavanh Phomvihane, Vietnamese Foreign Minister Le Hoai Trung and Myanmar's Minister for the Ministry of National Planning, Investment and Foreign Economic Relations, Aung Kyaw Hoe, attended the meeting here on Wednesday. (Xinhua/Tian Yu) BEIJING, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Wednesday called on the six Lancang-Mekong countries to build on their fruitful cooperation in the past 10 years and jointly usher in a new "golden decade." Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks when co-chairing with Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow the 11th Lancang-Mekong Cooperation (LMC) Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Beijing. The LMC mechanism was launched by the six countries in 2016. Its name derives from a river known as the Lancang in China and the Mekong after it flows out of the country and through Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam. China stands ready to work with Mekong countries in the direction set by the leaders, take stronger measures and more coordinated steps, to continuously substantiate the Lancang-Mekong community with a shared future, Wang said. Wang called for efforts to keep Lancang-Mekong Cooperation at the forefront of regional cooperation, make it a benchmark for Global South solidarity, and contribute to building a community with a shared future for humanity. Lancang-Mekong countries should strengthen top-level design on core issues such as regional development and security, enhance the alignment of development strategies, promote trade and investment liberalization and facilitation, and deliver more "small and beautiful" livelihood demonstration projects to give people a greater sense of gain, he said. It is important to expand cooperation in emerging fields such as the digital economy, artificial intelligence, smart manufacturing and smart agriculture, he said, welcoming more Mekong countries to join the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO). He urged Lancang-Mekong countries to oppose external interference and incitement of bloc confrontation, reject the creation of exclusive "small circles," and never allow the resurgence of militarism, adding that the countries should step up joint efforts to combat cross-border crimes. Wang suggested the countries promote the establishment of a Lancang-Mekong cross-border disaster early-warning cooperation mechanism and jointly enhance disaster prevention, mitigation and relief capabilities. Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn, Lao Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Thongsavanh Phomvihane, Vietnamese Foreign Minister Le Hoai Trung and Myanmar's Minister for the Ministry of National Planning, Investment and Foreign Economic Relations, Aung Kyaw Hoe, attended the meeting. All parties at the meeting spoke highly of the positive progress of the LMC over the past decade and appreciated China's important leading role in advancing their cooperation. Those present reaffirmed their commitment to good-neighborliness and friendship, mutual respect and mutual trust, deeper cooperation and win-win outcomes, and to jointly promoting sustainable development and prosperity in the region. They agreed to deepen cooperation in priority areas such as connectivity, water resources and environment, expand digital transformation, green innovation, and promote people-to-people and cultural exchanges. They also agreed to strengthen disaster governance, tighten security coordination, combat cross-border crimes and safeguard regional tranquility. All parties agreed to maintain close communication to ensure that the fifth LMC Leaders' Meeting is a complete success and delivers positive outcomes. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, co-chairs the 11th Lancang-Mekong Cooperation (LMC) Foreign Ministers' Meeting with Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 4, 2026. item.title: China's import expo draws more Fortune Global 500 companies, industry leaders
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
China's import expo draws more Fortune Global 500 companies, industry leaders This photo taken on Nov. 4, 2026 shows a view of the Hall 3 of the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) in Shanghai, east China. (Xinhua/Guo Lei) SHANGHAI, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- The numbers of overseas companies and industry heavyweights attending the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) are both set to reach record highs, underscoring the enduring appeal of the world's largest import-themed trade fair. The event is scheduled to open on Thursday in Shanghai, east China, with more than 300 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders expected to participate, marking a record high. Additionally, more than 2,000 companies will be exhibiting here for the first time, according to organizers. This year's expo is expected to attract a record 4,142 overseas exhibitors from 148 countries and regions. In total, 162 countries, regions and international organizations will participate, according to the Ministry of Commerce. Since its launch in 2018, the trade fair has maintained strong appeal for international companies of all sizes, which have used the platform as a launchpad for new products in China and a fast track to enter the world's second-largest consumer market. Danish pharmaceutical giant Novo Nordisk, which has participated in all the previous eight editions of the expo, will showcase new medicines during this year's event, including Kyinsu, a once-weekly injection for type 2 diabetes. "The CIIE has become an important part of our work in China," said Mike Doustdar, president and CEO of Novo Nordisk. "This is our ninth consecutive year taking part, and many medicines we first presented at the expo have since launched here." This year, over 480 exhibits are set to make their global, Asian or China debuts -- another record for the event. Canada-headquartered athletic apparel brand lululemon will participate in the trade fair for the third consecutive year, with China now serving as its second-largest market globally. "The CIIE is far more than a platform to showcase products," said San Yan Ng, regional president of lululemon China and APAC. "It also gives us the opportunity to engage in deeper dialogue and build stronger connections with Chinese guests, partners, government stakeholders and friends from all sectors." The CIIE is a prominent example of China's efforts to open its market wider and facilitate entry of quality products from around the world. China expects the expanded imports will boost domestic demands and support its industrial upgrading. The nation's imports reached 16.7 trillion yuan (about 2.48 trillion U.S. dollars) in the first nine months of this year, up 22.3 percent, the fastest growth since 2021. item.title: China voices concern over EU's new fees on low-value imports
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
Home>>
China voices concern over EU's new fees on low-value imports (Xinhua) 16:48, November 05, 2026 BEIJING, Nov. 5 (Xinhua) -- China is highly concerned about the European Union's (EU) new rule of imposing a 2-euro handling fee on low-value imports as of Nov. 1, following a 3-euro customs duty introduced in July this year, the Ministry of Commerce said on Thursday. Ministry spokesperson Huang Ling noted at a regular press conference that cross-border e-commerce, as a new business form and model of international trade, provides diversified choices for global enterprises and consumers. China hopes the EU will assess the impact of relevant policies in a prudent manner and create favorable conditions for China-EU cooperation in e-commerce and other fields, Huang said. item.title: Commentary: China bolsters confidence in building a shared green future
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
Commentary: China bolsters confidence in building a shared green future A drone photo taken on Jan. 13, 2026 shows the construction site of a 20-megawatt offshore wind turbine unit in the coastal waters of southeast China's Fujian Province. (Xinhua/Lin Shanchuan) BEIJING, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- In a world troubled by faltering climate policies, rising protectionism and energy security challenges, humanity, more than ever before, needs action-oriented implementation of the Paris Agreement. Since the entry into force of this milestone agreement a decade ago, China has made unwavering decarbonization endeavors and become an indispensable stabilizer and important contributor in advancing the global green transition process, bolstering confidence in a shared green future. This stabilizing role stems from China's efforts in managing its own affairs well, especially its clean energy buildout. China contributed nearly three-quarters of newly installed wind power capacity globally in 2025, International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) data showed. It is estimated that global photovoltaic installations added since 2019 avoided about 1.5 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions in 2025, with roughly half of this contribution coming from China. China's green transition momentum has been continuing. In 2025, China's carbon intensity further dropped by five percent from 2024 levels, and its power generation from renewable energy exceeded the total electricity consumption of the 27 EU member states. In July 2026, China's installed solar capacity, for the first time in its history, overtook coal-fired capacity, making solar its largest power source by installed capacity. China's achievements in pursuing green development represent an important contribution to global climate governance. Unquestionably, China has played a leading role in the global transition toward green and low-carbon development. The green transition requires not only resolve but, more importantly, affordable costs, accessible technologies and products suitable for widespread adoption. In this regard, China's contribution is tangible. According to IRENA, global wind and solar power costs have fallen by more than 60 percent and 80 percent, respectively, over the past decade, with much of this attributed to China's innovation, manufacturing and engineering endeavors. China has consistently worked to advance green cooperation, leveraging its technologies and investment in doing so. In South Africa, the Chinese-built Redstone solar plant helps ease electricity shortages. In the United Arab Emirates, meanwhile, a zero-energy cooling system using Chinese technology sharply reduces the energy consumption of buildings. According to a report by the Finland-based Center for Research on Energy and Clean Air, clean technology products exported by China in 2025 are expected to avoid approximately 6.9 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions during their operating lifetimes. Supported by strengths in battery technology, intelligent systems and supply-chain efficiency, Chinese new energy vehicle companies have built manufacturing and research facilities overseas, boosting global green transition and industrial upgrades in many developing countries. It is worth noting that no country can accomplish all transition-related tasks by relying solely on its own efforts. Countries need multilateralism and partnerships to effectively address the myriad challenges facing climate governance. This year, China has issued a raft of green development-related action plans, including those on carbon peaking and the establishment of a new power system, outlining concrete tasks and measures. These continued endeavors fully demonstrate that China is maintaining the intensity of its efforts via clear strategic goals and stable policy arrangements, which are set to generate new momentum for expanding green development cooperation and building a beautiful future. item.title: 9th China International Import Expo opens in Shanghai
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
9th China International Import Expo opens in Shanghai This photo taken on Nov. 5, 2026 shows a scene during the opening ceremony of the ninth edition of the China International Import Expo (CIIE) and the Hongqiao International Economic Forum in Shanghai, east China. The ninth edition of the CIIE opened on Thursday in Shanghai. (Xinhua/Fang Zhe) SHANGHAI, Nov. 5 (Xinhua) -- The ninth edition of the China International Import Expo (CIIE), the world's first national-level exhibition dedicated to imports, opened on Thursday in Shanghai in east China. Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang delivered a keynote speech at the opening ceremony. Running from Nov. 5 to 10, this year's CIIE has attracted 4,142 overseas exhibitors, including more than 300 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders. Over 480 exhibits are set to make their global, Asian or China debuts at the 2026 event, the highest number in its history. Total exhibition area exceeds 440,000 square meters this year. U.S. exhibitors occupy more than 50,000 square meters, leading for the eighth consecutive year, while companies from Germany, the United Kingdom and France also rank among the top participants. This year's CIIE retains its six major exhibition areas and an innovation incubation section, covering areas such as intelligent industry and information technology, consumer goods, food and agricultural products, automobiles and smart mobility, medical devices and healthcare products, and trade in services. The innovation incubation section features 633 technology and innovation projects from nearly 40 countries and regions, up almost 20 percent from the previous edition. The Hongqiao International Economic Forum, also taking place in Shanghai alongside the CIIE, on Thursday released the World Openness Report 2026, and unveiled its first Export-to-China Capacity Development Report. Announced in 2017 and held annually since 2018, the CIIE serves to give overseas businesses greater access to the vast and growing Chinese market. The past eight editions have drawn more than 180 countries, regions and international organizations and seen over 3,400 new products, technologies and services make their debuts, while cumulative intended deals have exceeded 580 billion U.S. dollars. item.title: World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit highlights China's open-source AI push
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit highlights China's open-source AI push HANGZHOU, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- At the physical workspace of ModelScope, China's largest AI open-source community, a single developer can do the work of a team. Li Guanghui is among the 249 solo entrepreneurs at this workspace in Hangzhou, capital city of east China's Zhejiang Province, 95 percent of whom are working on AI projects. A former developer at a major tech firm, he relocated to Hangzhou from Guangzhou in south China's Guangdong Province. With AI assistance, he built a hotel-booking mini program entirely on his own, completing in eight months a project that would typically take a team of five to ten people a year to finish. Li's experience reflects a broader trend being discussed at the ongoing 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit in Zhejiang's ancient water town of Wuzhen, highlighting how China's open-source push for an inclusive AI future is gaining momentum. The summit has drawn about 1,800 delegates from 138 countries and regions to discuss topics including open source and openness, joint contribution and shared benefits. This photo taken on Nov. 3, 2026 shows a scene at the opening ceremony of the 2026 World Internet Conference (WIC) Wuzhen Summit in Wuzhen, east China's Zhejiang Province. (Xinhua/Zhang Yuwei) "ModelScope now serves more than 33 million developers from 239 countries and regions," said Joe Tsai, co-founder and chairman of Alibaba Group, a Chinese tech giant that founded and operates ModelScope. "Through mutual inspiration, they are building a vibrant global ecosystem." Open source has become a defining feature of China's AI development. China's national-level AI open-source communities have attracted over 11 million users, while Chinese open-source large models have been downloaded more than 10 billion times globally. "Open source and openness are the foundation of the internet. Openness generates the massive data that fuels large models," said Ya-Qin Zhang, a foreign academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering. "Represented by Qwen and DeepSeek, China's open-source efforts are actively contributing to the global ecosystem." People visit the Open Source Ecosystem Experience Pavilion, a supporting project for the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit, in Wuzhen, east China's Zhejiang Province, Nov. 3, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Yuwei) Three years ago, Alibaba launched an open-source AI strategy. To date, its Qwen series has released more than 470 open-source models, featuring over 4 billion cumulative downloads and more than 330,000 derivative models worldwide. "AI can only become universal via open source, and only through universality can we create a sustainable and inclusive era of intelligence," said Tsai. He added that Chinese AI companies have converged on open source because it reflects China's innovation spirit: looking beyond self-interest, advancing shared well-being, and creating greater value through mutual achievement. "Why open source? The answer is simple: to bring artificial general intelligence closer, faster," said Gao Xi, a research engineer at China's AI startup DeepSeek. "Those who embrace open source benefit themselves." A person uses DeepSeek app on a mobile phone on Feb. 17, 2025. (Xinhua/Huang Zongzhi) Experts believe that open source is a key pathway to pooling intelligence and furthering digital inclusion. Practice shows that open source has lowered R&D costs for small and medium-sized enterprises, with particular value for less-used languages and developing countries. In Uganda, a non-profit organization built a local language model based on Qwen's open-source model, covering 68 African languages and helping more Africans break language barriers. Similar efforts using Chinese open-source AI models are emerging across Africa in sectors such as legal services, agriculture, education and insurance. "Based on open-source models, AI is no longer the exclusive domain of a few tech powers, but a cause that all can participate in," Tsai said. "Developers from emerging economies no longer need to start from scratch." People visit the Open Source Ecosystem Experience Pavilion, a supporting project for the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit, in Wuzhen, east China's Zhejiang Province, Nov. 3, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Yuwei) John Hoffman, chairman and director of the Global System for Mobile Communications Association (GSMA) Ltd., praised China's push for open technologies. "No openness, no scale; no cooperation, no inclusion," he told Xinhua, adding that openness gave the industry scale, lower costs and a connected world. "Openness is a simple word, but it carries a powerful message about how we develop technology, share knowledge and shape our common future in cyberspace," said Nii Narku Quaynor, chairman of Ghana Dot Com, also known as the "father of the internet in Africa." A visitor takes photos of a MAZU-FengYun satellite AI box during the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance in Shanghai, east China, July 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Haoming) Open-source AI is, notably, entering public services. China's Mazu intelligent weather early-warning system has been deployed in eight countries, including Pakistan, Ethiopia and Sri Lanka, with cloud trials underway in more than 50 countries as of October 2026. At the Wuzhen summit's exhibition area, a robot powered by Robbyant's LingBot embodied AI models picks up medicines in a simulated pharmacy. This solution, unveiled in July, is already in use at several pharmacies in Shanghai in east China. A visitor watches a robot powered by Robbyant's LingBot embodied AI models during the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance in Shanghai, east China, July 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Haoming) "China's open source efforts are moving from screens into the physical world," said Zhu Xing, CEO of Robbyant, an embodied AI company under Ant Group, noting that Robbyant's open-source models are increasingly used by overseas researchers as testbeds and starting points for new work. "Pharmacies carry medicines in many forms, bags, boxes, bottles and even transparent packages, placed densely in aisles only around 80 centimeters wide," said Duan Xiaoyue, a market operation specialist at Robbyant. Duan told Xinhua that this puts higher demands on the model's perception and motion planning. In real stores, the system also needs more robust dynamic obstacle avoidance when navigating around elderly customers, wheelchair users, children and pets. A staff member demonstrates a humanoid robot imitating the fine movements of human hands at the 2026 World Internet Conference (2026 WIC) Light of Internet Expo in Wuzhen, east China's Zhejiang Province, Nov. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Zongzhi) The company's LingBot embodied AI models, meanwhile, have been downloaded more than 2.2 million times within nine months, helping lower the entry cost for robotics developers. "Open source is not just about making code visible, but about replacing monopoly with collaboration and breaking boundaries through sharing," said Ni Xingjun, senior vice president of Ant Group and chairman of Ant Group's Technology Strategy Committee. Participants at the summit have also called for broader engagement and responsible development. Guests talk before the opening ceremony of the 2026 World Internet Conference (WIC) Wuzhen Summit in Wuzhen, east China's Zhejiang Province, Nov. 3, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Yun) Quaynor highlighted three dimensions of openness: open documents, open standards and meaningful participation, particularly from Africa and the Global South. Zhang advocated that companies investing in AI should allocate part of their AI budgets to AI governance research and urged jointly developing interoperability standards for AI agents and international safety evaluation platforms to ensure open-source benefits remain controllable and sustainable. "We hope open source can become basic public infrastructure in the digital world, where every participant, regardless of location or seniority, can contribute and benefit on an equal basis," Ni added. item.title: Foreign companies strengthen their footprint in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
Foreign companies strengthen their footprint in Shenzhen Photo shows a night view of the Houhai area in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province. (Photo/Leng Wen) At Qianhai in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province, the bonded maintenance center of German health tech company Siemens Healthineers provides global after-sales support for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) equipment. Simultaneously, next-generation digital elevator technology from Finnish manufacturer KONE is quickly reaching markets across the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. Foreign banks and financial institutions from the UK, Singapore, and elsewhere are establishing operations in the Qianhai Shenzhen-Hong Kong International Financial City. With its high degree of openness and strong economic vitality, Shenzhen continues to strengthen its appeal as a global investment destination. Throughout the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-2025), Shenzhen registered 44,000 new foreign-invested enterprises, and the volume of foreign investment actually utilized in the city surpassed 300 billion yuan (about $45.05 billion). More than 340 Fortune Global 500 companies have invested in the city. The latest figures show that Shenzhen's actual utilization of foreign investment exceeded 44 billion yuan in the first nine months of this year, up more than 60 percent year on year. "When I first came here more than a decade ago, workers were still lining the production lines," said Zhang Hongliang, vice president of operations for Flex's Industrial Products business in Asia-Pacific, beside an automated production line at Flextronics Electronics Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. Photo shows an intelligent manufacturing workshop at the Shenzhen factory of French auto parts maker Valeo. (Photo courtesy of Bao'an district, Shenzhen) Today, the facility is the company's only pilot "future factory" in Asia. Automated equipment, integrated digital systems, and AI algorithms drive its production lines, doubling productivity per employee. In the early years of reform and opening-up, Shenzhen's flexible policies as a special economic zone and convenient port access attracted large numbers of foreign manufacturers. In 1987, Flex, a technology company founded in Silicon Valley in the U.S., established its first factory in the Chinese mainland in Shekou, Shenzhen. The company has continued to expand its investment in the city ever since. "Shenzhen's highly efficient supply chains, robust digital ecosystem, and proactive government support for technological upgrades have laid a solid foundation for the company's transition to intelligent manufacturing," Zhang said. The achievements made in Shenzhen are now being rapidly replicated across Flex's manufacturing facilities worldwide. As Shenzhen steps up efforts to build a world-class automotive hub, French auto parts maker Valeo is becoming increasingly integrated into the local automotive industry chain, advancing technological upgrades and optimizing production in intelligent driving and smart cockpit systems. "China is no longer just the world's largest automotive market. It has also become a global 'fitness center' for the automotive industry and a demanding testing ground," said Zhou Song, president of Valeo China. Around 30 percent of the value of intelligent connected vehicles comes from the information technology industry, which aligns closely with Shenzhen's industrial foundation and innovation ecosystem, Zhou added. Citizens and visitors enjoy a stroll along the waterfront promenade at Shenzhen Bay Park in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province. (Photo/Ran Guangjun) At Siemens Healthineers' Shenzhen base, more than a dozen MRI systems stand in rows as they undergo final testing before being shipped to Australia, Japan, Thailand and other markets. By the end of 2025, the facility had delivered more than 10,000 MRI and angiography equipment to over 120 countries and regions. Siemens Healthineers established its Shenzhen operations in 2002. Back then, China's medical device industry was still in its early stages. An MRI system involves thousands of components, and a local supply chain was yet to be established. "We have remained committed to localizing our operations and helped develop more than 300 local suppliers. Locally sourced components now account for 80 percent of our finished products," said Ma Tianshi, general manager of Siemens Shenzhen Magnetic Resonance Ltd. "We remain committed to investing in Shenzhen and deepening our presence in China, strengthening our intelligent manufacturing capabilities to serve both the Chinese and global markets," said Ma. As more foreign companies establish and expand their operations in Shenzhen, the city is evolving from a manufacturing base into an important center for global innovation. In the first half of this year, foreign investment in actual use in Shenzhen's high-tech industries accounted for more than 70 percent of the city's total utilized foreign investment. The city is now home to more than 200 foreign-funded R&D centers, employing over 30,000 researchers. In March this year, KONE officially opened its southern China headquarters in Qianhai. "KONE's presence in China has evolved from sales and manufacturing to R&D and, more recently, innovation," said Xie Jijun, senior vice president of KONE Greater China. The company is now introducing digital, green and energy-efficient technologies in the Chinese market before taking them global. The rapid growth of emerging and future industries in Shenzhen is also drawing international financial institutions to the city. HSBC Bank (China) Co., Ltd. has set up a team in Shenzhen to provide financial services for technology and innovation companies. The team focuses on cross-border fintech innovation in the Greater Bay Area and has launched a range of innovative products that leverage digital technology and are tailored to the needs of technology and innovation companies. "This reflects our confidence in Shenzhen's technology and innovation companies and its emerging industries, as well as our commitment to supporting their growth," said Li Qile, general manager for the Greater Bay Area at HSBC Bank (China) Co., Ltd. Shenzhen has consistently worked to attract and utilize high-quality foreign investment while further opening up its economy. In December 2025, the city introduced measures to further attract and utilize foreign investment, strengthening policy support for opening up key sectors, improving the business environment and facilitating investment. Going forward, Shenzhen will actively advance institutional opening-up and develop itself into a high-level international trade hub, said an official from the Investment Promotion Bureau of Shenzhen Municipality. item.title: Qinzhou: Bridging rivers and seas, opening to the world

Published: 2026-11-05
Qinzhou: Bridging rivers and seas, opening to the world Photo shows an aerial view of Longmen Bridge in Qinzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region. (Photo/Chu Naiqin) Situated on the Beibu Gulf coast in south China's Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region, Qinzhou has served as a maritime gateway since ancient times, linking inland waterways with the open sea. Today, propelled by the expansion of the Beibu Gulf International Gateway Port, the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, and the China-Malaysia Qinzhou Industrial Park, the city is forging a dynamic new path toward deeper maritime engagement and global integration. A modern maritime hub: Streamlining connectivity and multimodal transport At the automated container terminal of Beibu Gulf Port, cargo operations run continuously around the clock. Nearby, at a bulk cargo berth, the vessel Dubai Nature -- carrying imported soybeans -- has just docked. On deck, Bangladeshi crew member Rajib oversees mooring operations. Watching giant vessels pass one after another along the channel, he said: "The port is spacious. Operations run in an orderly manner, and the staff are friendly and responsible. It has left a deep impression on me." Qinzhou Port currently has 96 operational berths, including berths capable of accommodating vessels of up to 300,000 tonnes. It operates 92 container shipping routes, connecting with more than 200 ports in over 100 countries and regions worldwide. In June this year, Moiz Farooq, executive editor of Pakistan Economic Network, visited Qinzhou. At the Smart Port Innovation Center of Beibu Gulf, he watched demonstrations of smart port operations, including the precise dispatching of autonomous container trucks. "Qinzhou has world-class port facilities, and landmark projects such as the Pinglu Canal give it outstanding advantages in developing foreign trade," Farooq said. "I hope to see more Pakistani companies come to Qinzhou and explore cooperation opportunities in areas such as logistics, port development, maritime trade, and the digital economy." Photo shows an aerial view of the Madao hub on the Pinglu Canal in Lingshan county, Qinzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region. (Photo courtesy of Pinglu Canal Group) On September 16, the landmark Pinglu Canal opened for navigation. "The waterway establishes a new link between the inland waterway network and the sea, effectively shortening transport distances and reducing costs. It will also spur industrial clustering and port-related economic development in Qinzhou, enhancing regional competitiveness," said Philippe Gourbesville, president of the International Association for Hydro-Environment Engineering and Research, after visiting the canal. Fostering industrial growth and streamlining business services To support business development, Qinzhou has set up dedicated service teams at both municipal and county levels to assist enterprises in the real economy. Staff members regularly visit businesses and follow up on concerns raised through online platforms, providing ongoing support to help businesses resolve operational difficulties. Han Seong Woo, a South Korean manager at Guangxi Lingshan Delin Toys Co., Ltd. in Lingshan county, Qinzhou, once encountered difficulties with identity verification when applying to change his company's business address. Recognizing the complexity, staff members promptly coordinated across departments and guided him through the necessary steps. What he anticipated would be a lengthy bureaucratic process was resolved efficiently. Thanks to multiple opening-up platforms, including the China-Malaysia Qinzhou Industrial Park and the Qinzhou Port area of the China (Guangxi) Pilot Free Trade Zone, Qinzhou is now home to 211 foreign-invested enterprises. Foreign-funded projects in light industry, aquatic products and port-related industries are steadily being implemented, injecting fresh impetus into local development. "Qinzhou offers not only a highly supportive business environment but also a rich historical and cultural heritage. Lingshan county, for example, is home to ancient buildings such as those in the ancient Dalu Village," Han said. "As Qinzhou continues to open up, it will attract more South Koreans to work and invest here, further strengthening economic, trade and cultural ties between South Korea and China," he added. Bridging cultures through education and people-to-people exchange Inside a classroom at Beibu Gulf University in Qinzhou, students practice conversational Thai under the guidance of instructor Orawee Wei. Standing beside their desks, she uses expressive gestures to help learners master intonation and rhythm. "After living in Qinzhou for many years, I have come to regard this place as my second home," she said. Over recent years, schools in Qinzhou have established sister-school partnerships with their counterparts in Malaysia and other ASEAN countries, organizing a range of people-to-people exchange activities, including cultural and tourism exchange activities and study programs for young people. Wei, who grew up in a family of teachers in Nakhon Sawan province, Thailand, joined Beibu Gulf University in 2020. "When I first arrived, only 80 students were studying Thai. Today, that number has grown to more than 200, with an increasing number of young Chinese people eager to learn the language," she said. Journalists from ASEAN countries visit the Qinzhou automated container terminal of Beibu Gulf Port in Qinzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region. (Photo/Liang Sheng) Wei teaches specialized courses such as Business Thai and Practical Thai for International Trade. She has seen five cohorts of her students graduate. "My students are actively involved in Thailand-China economic and trade exchanges. They work as accompanying interpreters, business secretaries and foreign trade accountants for Thai and Chinese companies, helping strengthen economic and trade ties between Qinzhou and ASEAN," she said. From an ancient port once bustling with sailing ships to a modern gateway now traversed by giant vessels, Qinzhou has become a key hub of the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor. Linking mountains and seas and creating opportunities, the city keeps goods moving, businesses thriving and people connected, offering a vivid example of cooperation and exchanges between China and the rest of the world. Representatives of Malaysian students in China pose for a group photo with Chinese students at the Experimental School in the Qinzhou Port Economic and Technological Development Zone in Qinzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region. item.title: Embracing the trend of openness and pooling strength for win-win cooperation

Published: 2026-11-05
Embracing the trend of openness and pooling strength for win-win cooperation An exhibitor poses for a photo at the venue for the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) on Nov. 3, 2026. (Photo/Wang Chu) The 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) opens in Shanghai on Nov. 5 and will run through Nov. 10. This year's exhibition space exceeds 370,000 square meters for the first time, drawing participants from 162 countries, regions, and international organizations. More than 4,100 overseas companies are participating, and over 480 products are expected to make their debut at the expo, hitting a record high. At a time when unilateralism and protectionism continue to disrupt the international economic and trade order, the CIIE, now in its ninth consecutive year, has become an irreplaceable international public good in the global economic and trade system. A closer look at the exhibition layout of the 9th CIIE reveals six major exhibition areas and an Innovation Incubation Special Section, each with its own highlights. Pavilions dedicated to medical equipment and health care products, consumer goods, and food and agricultural products have all been expanded. More than 2,000 companies are participating in the event for the first time. Among the newcomers are the U.S.-based Project Management Institute and Germany's Caparol, a leading producer of architectural coatings. For the first time, the CIIE will feature a global consumer brands showcase to help expand and upgrade consumption of quality products. "The CIIE stands as a clear demonstration of China's commitment to expand opening up," said Carl Fey, professor of strategy at BI Norwegian Business School. As he has observed, China's opening up is geared toward pursuing shared development with the rest of the world, and the CIIE highlights China's key role in global trade. Over the years, the range of exhibits at the CIIE has expanded from consumer goods and components to high-end equipment, core technologies, and quality services. This evolution reflects the deeper integration of global industrial and supply chains. Today, exhibitors, including industry giants, emerging players, small and medium-sized enterprises, and specialized businesses, can all connect with market demand more precisely and explore growth opportunities across the entire industrial chain. The CIIE is increasingly attracting international buyers. Ahead of this year's event, trade delegations from Shanghai, Guangdong, and other regions secured a number of major buyers with strong purchasing power, well-established brands, and substantial demand. Photo shows the Intelligent Industry and Information Technology exhibition area at the venue for the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE), Nov. 3, 2026. (Photo/Wang Chu) Dedicated matchmaking events were held in Egypt, Germany, the UK, and other countries, bringing negotiations closer to China's trading partners. During the expo, a buyers' corridor will help connect quality products and services directly with the Chinese market. In the first three quarters of 2026, China's imports reached 16.74 trillion yuan (about $2.5 trillion), representing a 22.3 percent year-on-year increase. September alone saw monthly imports surpass 2 trillion yuan for the first time. The CIIE offers a window into China's vast domestic market, where growing demand is creating more opportunities for business around the world. The expo is also becoming an increasingly attractive platform for foreign investors. Through the CIIE, exhibitors including ZEISS Group, Schneider Electric and AstraZeneca have established R&D centers, regional headquarters and advanced manufacturing bases in China. As global companies unveil debut products, many are simultaneously accelerating plans to deepen local R&D, increase investment, and consolidate regional operations. Over the past three years, the number of foreign-invested enterprises in China has grown steadily. Between January and April 2026 alone, more than 3,000 foreign-invested firms announced additional capital commitments. The CIIE continues to witness how exhibits become marketable products and exhibitors become investors, and more global companies deepen their presence in China and create benefits for the world. Beyond commerce, the expo is strengthening cultural and people-to-people ties. More than a marketplace for goods and services, it serves as a cross-cultural forum. The distinctive Country Exhibition area hosts performances and exhibitions that offer visitors a rich tapestry of global traditions. This year introduces several firsts: the Premium Collection will feature intangible cultural heritage workshops, the Gourmet Festival will launch a global tasting zone, and the Arts Carnival will collaborate with China Fashion Week. These initiatives foster mutual understanding and enrich economic partnerships with stronger societal connections. A staff member debugs a humanoid robot at the venue for the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE). (Photo/Wang Chu) The CIIE provides a broader multilateral platform for open cooperation. In step with the trend of economic globalization, it has established an authoritative platform for high-level dialogue and multilateral economic and trade cooperation. For the first time, more than 300 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders are participating. Nearly 200 firms and institutions have attended all nine editions, while five countries, including Moldova and Romania, as well as the United Nations Development Programme, are joining for the first time, demonstrating the strong appeal of openness and cooperation. China advances high-level opening up with the aim of expanding the pie of cooperation with the rest of the world. Its stories of opening up have sent a message to the world that China is not only the world's factory but also a global market. It is not only a "super seller" but also a "super buyer." The two-way engagement does not marginalize other stakeholders; rather, it creates tangible benefits for neighboring economies and fosters regional prosperity. At this year's expo, pavilions dedicated to Asian and African products will be expanded, featuring higher-quality displays and enhanced programming. These enhancements aim to help African countries with diplomatic ties to China leverage tariff-free access and encourage more Global South countries to fully utilize the CIIE. Stephen Jackson, United Nations Resident Coordinator in China, noted that the CIIE offers developing economies a practical pathway to integrate more deeply into global value chains and share the benefits of trade. China will harness the momentum of opening up and pool strength for win-win cooperation. It will firmly uphold multilateralism and continue to make the CIIE a success, helping steer economic globalization toward greater openness, inclusiveness, balance and shared benefits.
